title: Adaptive stream handshake and failure isolation for Python SDK streaming chat
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem statement: Python SDK users implementing streaming chat often need a small set of guarantees: simple handshake to establish event schema, the ability to resume from partial fragments, deterministic fragment reconciliation on resume, and local failure isolation so one misbehaving handler or transient network spike doesn't take down the entire consumer. Current SDK primitives require significant user plumbing (manual token checkpoints, bespoke retries, and brittle fragment assembly).

Goal: Provide an ergonomic, opt-in surface for streaming chat that: (1) performs a lightweight handshake to negotiate event shape & server capabilities, (2) exposes a resume_token + checkpoint API that is safe for concurrent use, (3) offers built-in fragment reconciliation with configurable heuristics (time-based, sequence gaps, explicit end-of-fragment markers), and (4) isolates downstream handler failures with supervisor semantics so retries/backoff affect only the failing fragment or handler, not the whole client connection.

Scope: Python SDK only (first iteration). Implementation includes new high-level ChatStream class, a small compatibility shim for existing low-level stream consumers, example cookbooks, unit + integration tests against streaming sandbox, and telemetry hooks for handshake success/failure, resume events, fragment drop rate, and handler exception rates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New ChatStream can be created with a one-line call that accepts a handler callback or async iterator. 2) ChatStream exposes .checkpoint() that returns a resume_token; calling .resume(resume_token) returns a stream at the nearest fragment boundary and replays any uncommitted content. 3) If a handler raises, only that fragment is retried with exponential backoff and bounded attempts; the rest of the stream continues. 4) Fragment reconciliation succeeds for out-of-order partial fragments using fragment_id + seq heuristics. 5) SDK emits telemetry events for handshake, resume, fragment_reconcile_{success|fail}, handler_retry_{attempt|giveup}.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: use a two-step handshake (client metadata -> server capabilities) so client can enable automatic fragment markers and server-provided resume checkpoints when available. Resume tokens are opaque strings but include a server-signed cursor plus client-side checksum. Checkpointing is cheap (no blocking IO) and safe to call from concurrent tasks.

Fragment model: each chat stream fragment carries fragment_id, seq (monotonic within fragment), and end_of_fragment boolean. The reconciler will buffer at most N partial fragments (configurable, default 4) and apply idempotent reassembly based on (fragment_id, seq). On resume, we align to the last committed fragment_id; partial fragments with conflicting content will be emitted as reconciliation warnings and dropped after one retry unless user opts-in to manual merge callback.

Failure isolation: wrap user handlers in a Supervisor that captures exceptions, schedules a fragment-local retry with jittered backoff (base=100ms, max=5s, attempts=3 default). If retries exhaust, emit handler_retry_giveup telemetry and continue. To avoid head-of-line blocking, retries occur out-of-band while the stream ack mechanism marks fragment as "pending_reconcile"; server fallback semantics are used if the server signals cancel for that fragment.

API sketch (user-facing):

from redwood import ChatStream

async def on_event(evt):
    if evt.type == "delta":
        print(evt.text)
    elif evt.type == "fragment_end":
        await store.checkpoint(await stream.checkpoint())

stream = ChatStream.create(model="rw-light-8k", conv=conversation)
stream.subscribe(on_event)  # supports async callables or sync callables
await stream.start()

# Resume example:
resume = last_saved_token
stream = ChatStream.resume(resume)
await stream.start()

Backward compat: provide ChatStream.from_lowlevel(stream_adapter) that adapts older streaming responses to the new fragment model. The adapter will emit best-effort fragment ids derived from chunk offsets when server lacks fragment_id support.

Telemetry & Logs: integrate with sdk telemetry facade (span.events) and export these keys: sdk.stream.handshake, sdk.stream.resume, sdk.stream.fragment_reconcile, sdk.stream.handler_retry. Include structured fields: model, region, resume_present (bool), fragment_count, reconcile_time_ms, handler_attempts.

Compatibility knobs: users can set StreamPolicy to adjust max_buffered_fragments, retry_attempts, soft_ack_timeout, and reconcile_strategy (strict | tolerant | manual).
tests: Unit tests: fragment reassembly deterministic cases, concurrent checkpoint calls, handler exception -> retry semantics, resume token roundtrip. Integration tests: run streaming sandbox with simulated jitter/dropped packets and validate resume and reconcilation behavior. E2E cookbook test: example app that displays incremental messages, simulates handler exceptions, and resumes using saved tokens. Add fuzz test that shuffles chunk orders to validate buffering heuristics. CI: add a new 'streaming' integration matrix job that spins up local sandbox and runs representative scenarios.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Asha Menon: Triage complete. This addresses a recurring customer support pattern where users botch resume and fragment merges. Initial design proposed.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Liam O'Connor): Reviewed fragment model and supervisor semantics. Asked to tighten default retry attempts from 5->3 and add telemetry for reconcile failures.
2026-03-07 - Implementation: Started ChatStream skeleton and low-level adapter. WIP branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/894
2026-03-10 - QA: Added unit tests for reassembly. Observed a race when .checkpoint() called concurrently; fixed by using an asyncio.Lock around token generation.
2026-03-14 - PR updated: Added integration tests against streaming sandbox. Requesting review from @marina and @devops for telemetry schema and CI job resources.
